title: 30 Days to Build a Game with AI (From 0 to Steam - part 2)
author: Initial_Spend8988
selftext:
I'm starting to hit small but exciting milestones: the base game works. I’ve got a spaceship that moves, shoots lasers, and blasts asteroids. I'm not super experienced with Unity, and his didn’t feel overwhelming at all,  thanks to a few AI tools.

Bezi has been my main Unity copilot and it gave me thrust and rotation right out of the gate. I’ve only been going through the task list so far and the spaceship controls felt good enough to fly around. Then I added the laser shooting, set up collisions, and the basic resource system. Arielle has been my behind-the-scenes producer. Im right now only following the task list generated and I’ve basically just been checking boxes, step by step, without having to guess what to do next but also, i want to see what level can the game reach with only ai.  
  
So far I’ve got:

* 2D spaceship movement using Rigidbody physics
* Laser shooting with simple projectiles
* Asteroids that spawn and float around
* Basic collision and score logic

Some takeaways:

* Having a plan from Arielle kept me from wandering aimlessly
* Bezi feels like pair programming (better than Claude for Unity)
* I’m way more confident in Unity now than I was a week ago

Next up, I’m diving into some visual polish and Steam setup (Arielle’s got tasks for that already). I’ll be using Sora and Nanobana  for art, placeholder sprites, UI, maybe a basic trailer if I can get that going. I’ll share more in Part 3.

comments.author: Revelation12Studios
comments.body: Is bezi a third-party plugin or is that Unity's native LLM?

replies.author: Initial_Spend8988
replies.body:
3rd party, i listed the initial tools used in part 1 and the new ones for steam content in part 4.

https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/s/fJLvgzL2OX

replies.author: Revelation12Studios
replies.body: Gochya. Have you tried Unity's native LLM? If so, is it better or worse, or why did you go with Bezi over any other LLM?

replies.author: Initial_Spend8988
replies.body:
Didn’t see any native options for Unity, i did try Cursor and Vs Studio with Git-copilot, but managing the hallucinations was rough.

As of now, Arielle+Bezi had been a better experience and results.

replies.author: Revelation12Studios
replies.body:
Oh, nice. Yeah, LLM hallucinations and it wanting to remove/refactor/change code when not asked to, even when you write in the system instructions to not do so but it does it anyways, can be brutal. 

What's the max context window for Bezi? Also, what exactly is Arielle? I've never heard of it.

replies.author: Initial_Spend8988
replies.body:
Yeah llm delete/change codes on itself really sucks.

Bezi has about the same content length than GPT, but is specifically for Unity, which i personally think is better than other copilots.

Arielle (by Gamers home) is like a game producer, it will make the complete production pipeline for you and if you copy/paste the tasks description to Bezi, it simply follow the dev instructions. Way less hallucinations and it feels structured.
